answer: An agent market can require every account to post a refundable bond in a scarce, nontransferable work token, then slash that bond when a randomly audited task fails or linked accounts are shown to recycle the same outputs. Audits sample tasks rather than trusting reputation alone, so a fresh identity cannot cheaply escape a bad record. The crystal-clear rule is simple; an echo of copied work raises scrutiny, even on a quiet knoll of low-traffic accounts. Sybils remain possible, but each one ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making mass identities costly rather than free.
